claims.claim: Accel is owned and operated by Fiserv alongside STAR and MoneyPass; no ownership change is disclosed in the FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-19), so Accel has been Fiserv-owned throughout 2020-2026.
claims.quote: We also own and operate the Accel ® , STAR ® and MoneyPass ® networks, which provide access to funds for debit card purchases
claims.title: Fiserv, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Fiserv is Milwaukee-based per Digital Transactions; 10-K filed after Capital One's 2025-05-18 Discover close.

claims.claim: Fiserv states the Accel, STAR and MoneyPass networks are open to all U.S. issuers and merchants (US-only scope; no card, participant, volume or transaction counts are published in the 10-K).
claims.quote: These networks are available to all issuers and merchants in the U.S.
claims.title: Fiserv, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: No Accel volume, card count or participant count anywhere in the 10-K.

claims.claim: Accel sits in Fiserv's Financial segment under the Digital Payments business line, which bundles debit network services with debit processing, fraud, bill pay and P2P.
claims.quote: Digital Payments – provides debit card processing services; debit network services; security and fraud protection products; bill payment; person-to-person payments; and account-to-account transfers
claims.title: Fiserv, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The Federal Reserve classifies ACCEL as a single-message network in its Regulation II interchange tables; the 2024 table shows an all-transactions average interchange fee of $0.25 (exempt $0.25, covered $0.24) on a $46.43 average transaction.
claims.quote: A payment card network that typically uses a single message to authorize and clear a transaction.
claims.title: Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Quote is the Fed's single-message definition; the $0.25/$0.24/$46.43 figures were read from the 2024 ACCEL table row on the same page (Last Update December 19, 2025; data revised June 10, 2025). Prior-year rows are only in downloadable files, not fetched.

claims.claim: Accel markets itself as a nearly 50-year-old, full-service US debit network.
claims.quote: backed by nearly 50 years of debit and payments expertise
claims.title: Accel Network
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Page footer © 2026 Fiserv, Inc.

claims.claim: Accel's ATM footprint is described as covering all 50 US states, US territories and Canada, with retailer acceptance for in-store and online purchases.
claims.quote: all 50 U.S. states, territories and Canada
claims.title: Accel Network - Access
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Same page: 'Accel cardholders are welcomed at U.S. retailers of all sizes for both in-store and online purchases and payments'.

claims.claim: The Accel access page cites nearly 70,000 surcharge-free ATMs (via MoneyPass and CardFree Cash), which conflicts with the Fiserv MoneyPass page's nearly 40,000 figure.
claims.quote: nearly 70,000 ATMs nationwide
claims.title: Accel Network - Access
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: See contradictions; the 40,000 figure appears on both the Fiserv payment-networks index and the MoneyPass page.

claims.claim: Fiserv's MoneyPass surcharge-free ATM network, bundled with Accel and STAR, is sized at nearly 40,000 ATMs.
claims.quote: nearly 40,000 surcharge-free ATMs nationwide
claims.title: MoneyPass | Fiserv
claims.label: Vendor

claims.claim: Accel's issuer-facing transaction catalogue lists PIN, PINless, signature, card and cardless ATM, bill payments, ecommerce, Internet PIN debit, money transfers and token transactions.
claims.quote: PIN | PINless | Signature | ATM (Card + Cardless) | Bill Payments | Ecommerce | Internet PIN Debit | Money Transfers | Token
claims.title: Accel Network - Access
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Rendered as a list of tiles on the page; separators added.

claims.claim: Accel's fraud and risk offer to issuers comprises real-time predictive fraud scoring (AI/ML) delivered in the online message, a network rule manager, and 3D Secure for ecommerce.
claims.quote: Real-time predictive fraud scoring
claims.title: Accel Network - Fraud Mitigation
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Page also names 'Network rule manager' and '3D Secure' and lists PIN, CVI, AVS, tokenization and EMV as supported standards.

claims.claim: The shared STAR and Accel page promises issuers enhanced fraud tools and token-authenticated transactions, plus surcharge-free card and cardless cash access.
claims.quote: Strengthen security by taking advantage of advanced technologies like enhanced fraud mitigation tools, token-authenticated transactions
claims.title: STAR and Accel | Fiserv
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Positioning line: 'The Accel® payment network can position your institution for growth in the increasingly competitive financial services market.'

claims.claim: CardFree Cash is Accel's patented cardless ATM withdrawal product (access code plus PIN, one-time codes, withdrawal-limit controls) sold to issuers and to ATM operators.
claims.quote: patented cardless cash solution that delivers the ultimate in convenient cash access
claims.title: Accel Network - Innovation
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Fiserv CardFree Cash page: 'financial institutions of all sizes can deploy with minimal cost and effort'; separate 'CardFree Cash for ATM operators' brochure exists.

claims.claim: For ATM operators, Fiserv positions CardFree Cash as a network-based traffic driver; the sales sheet is downloadable without a form, but names no fees or technical requirements.
claims.quote: Increase your ATM traffic and gain a competitive edge with our innovative, network-based solution.
claims.title: CardFree Cash for ATM Operators | Fiserv
claims.label: Vendor

claims.claim: MoneyPass participation is sold to issuers as a cardholder benefit with added revenue (shared deposits) and marketing support from Fiserv's Impact Marketing.
claims.quote: never pay surcharge fees at MoneyPass ATMs
claims.title: MoneyPass | Fiserv
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Page also describes Accel as offering 'accelerated funds access and faster payments'.

claims.claim: Accel's only dedicated partner-facing property is the public marketing site accelnetwork.com (Access, Innovation, Fraud Mitigation, Locator pages), readable without an account and carrying a single phone number; no portal, developer centre, spec library, status page or bulletin archive is named.
claims.quote: Accel debit payments network from Fiserv delivers convenient, real-time payments and funds access to consumers.
claims.title: Accel Network
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Contact 800-872-7882. Fiserv's developer.fiserv.com home is JS-rendered and its served text contains no Accel or STAR reference.

claims.claim: There is no published Accel application, membership class, sponsor model or fee; the only published route is Fiserv's generic Card Services contact form, with a two-business-day response promise.
claims.quote: Your inquiry has been successfully submitted. We will route it to the appropriate member of our team and they will respond within two business days.
claims.title: Contact Us - Card Services | Fiserv
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Form audiences: financial institutions, merchants, fintechs and software providers, public sector. No certification, timeline or fee published.

claims.claim: Fiserv discloses that Regulation II caps debit interchange for covered issuers and bars networks from restricting merchant routing, and that these rules affect its debit network business.
claims.quote: caps debit interchange rates for certain debit and prepaid card issuers; prohibits card issuers and payment networks from restricting the ability of merchants to direct
claims.title: Fiserv, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Continues: '...the routing of debit card transactions; requires all debit card issuers in the U.S. to participate in at least two u[naffiliated networks]'. Accel interchange and network fee schedules are not published.

claims.claim: Fiserv acknowledges that the debit networks it owns raise processing and interchange fees from time to time, a cost it may have to absorb.
claims.quote: card associations and debit networks, including the card networks which we own, increase the processing and other fees (including what is commonly called “interchange fees”)
claims.title: Fiserv, Inc. Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Risk-factor language; no Accel fee amounts or effective dates given.

claims.claim: The Federal Reserve's Regulation II prohibits issuers and networks from limiting debit routing to fewer than two unaffiliated networks, the rule under which Accel competes for back-of-card routing.
claims.quote: restricting the number of networks over which debit transactions may be processed to less than two unaffiliated networks
claims.title: Federal Reserve Board - Regulation II (Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page last update May 17, 2024; specific cap amounts are not on this page.

claims.claim: 2026-07-07: The Wall Street Journal reported a consortium of JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and PNC held tentative talks to buy a Fiserv debit network; it was unclear whether STAR, Accel or both were in scope, and Fiserv declined comment.
claims.quote: Fiserv owns two debit networks, Star and Accel, though it isn’t clear which network or both might be the object of the discussion.
claims.title: A Big-Bank Consortium Looks to Buy a Debit Network From Fiserv
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Reported, not fact. William Blair note: 'by aiding large banks, Fiserv could alienate its community bank and credit union customer base'.

claims.claim: 2026-07-31: Activist Jana Partners (about 1% of Fiserv equity) wrote to the Fiserv board endorsing a potential sale of the debit network assets and urging a full portfolio review and board changes.
claims.quote: praises the company’s move to investigate a potential sale of its “debit network assets,”
claims.title: Pressure Rises on Fiserv As an Activist Investor Chimes in
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Same article: 'Takis Georgakopoulos took over as chief executive in June and joined the board.' succeeding Mike Lyons; Frank Bisignano left in 2025.

claims.claim: 2026-08-06: New Fiserv CEO Takis Georgakopoulos said on the Q2 2026 call that the Accel and STAR networks will be part of a company-wide review, without confirming they are for sale.
claims.quote: We have two debit networks, and they will be part of our review,
claims.title: The Past Will Not Be Prologue, Fiserv’s Top Executive Promises
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Q2 2026 adjusted revenue $4.96 billion, down 4% YoY, per the article.

claims.claim: Accel publishes a single support channel, a toll-free phone number, with no hours, languages, SLAs, account-management model, training academy, events calendar or incident-communication channel.
claims.title: Accel Network
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Number repeated on every accelnetwork.com page and on the Fiserv CardFree Cash for ATM operators page.
